title: Export redacted development events for honest cross-environment monitoring

requirement.summary: Let a user explicitly create a portable, privacy-bounded development-event bundle and let the Monitor distinguish exported development history from CI replay history.

objective.rationale: Local events are intentionally ignored by default, so CI cannot honestly claim development-time visibility unless a user explicitly exports a redacted, validated bundle.

goal: Implement an explicit metadata-only development-event export and support exported_development and combined Monitor scopes without overstating history completeness or governance effect.
non_goals: Do not automatically upload events, modify GitHub Actions, add central telemetry, or publish a package or release.
Do not export code, prompts, validation output, absolute paths, credentials, actor labels, or local evidence pointers.
Do not claim complete history, cross-stage discovery, requirement correctness, causal benefit, or return on investment.
Do not add approval, exception, commit, merge, deployment, hook, daemon, or governance-file write authority.
acceptance_signals: A strict export contract validates immutable metadata-only bundles and verifies their canonical event digest and derived interval/count fields.
Export rejects CI events, malformed or sensitive local records, symlinks, paths outside the repository, tracked outputs, existing outputs, and silent overwrite.
Export removes actor labels and local evidence references while retaining bounded actor class, task identity, governance references, reason codes, outcomes, and small counters.
The CLI previews the exact redaction and source counts without writing, and requires explicit confirmation before creating the bundle.
Monitor accepts exported_development from one validated export and combined from that export plus CI-only replay events, labels every timeline event by source, and reports source-specific counts.
All four observation scopes remain partial and cross-stage discovery remains unavailable because no cross-stage finding identity exists.
Focused contract, policy, CLI, schema, rendering, and documentation tests pass, followed by the complete suite and repository governance checks.
validation_commands: python -m unittest tests.test_development_event_export tests.test_development_monitor tests.test_event_store tests.test_portfolio_docs -v

items: A portable bundle could disclose development metadata if redaction is incomplete.
A combined Monitor could imply complete or causally linked cross-stage history when only two partial sources are visible.
An export writer could overwrite tracked or user-owned content without strict path and ownership controls.

stop_conditions: Stop if export safety would require retaining free-form text, source content, validation output, or absolute paths.
Stop if combined history cannot distinguish development export events from CI replay events.
Stop if implementation requires automatic upload, external telemetry, a workflow mutation, or expanded merge/deployment authority.
Stop if a deterministic integrity or privacy boundary cannot be covered by policy fixtures.

decision.rationale: The user explicitly asked to continue the corrected development-governance plan after the installed-build pilot.
